# IR Letter Report Spec-Compliance Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Bring the "Integrated Requirements" (IR) letter PDF — generated by the Quarkus backend at `~/Downloads/Misc/agwa-planning` and downloaded from the Angular `wwell-ir` feature — into compliance with the rules in `docs/ir-report/ir-report-download.md`.

**Architecture:** Nearly all changes live in the **agwa-planning** Quarkus backend: the DTO (`IrLetterData`), the assembler (`IrLetterDataAssembler`, where all display-formatting and the new required-field validation lives), a new blocking exception, and the Qute template (`irLetter.html`, restyled and restructured). The wellbore diagram's legend and revision block are added to the backend template around the client-supplied PNG image, not to the D3 SVG itself — but the legend's "Cement" and "Screen" swatches label patterns that, per Task 8's investigation, don't actually exist yet in the client-rendered diagram image (see Global Constraints). No other Angular-Practice frontend changes are required.

**Tech Stack:** Java 21, Quarkus, Qute templates, iText pdfHTML (`html2pdf`), JUnit 5 (plain unit tests, no Mockito/`@QuarkusTest` — matches this codebase's existing test convention).

**Spec:** `/Users/junedalam/angular-with-ngrx/Angular-Practice/docs/ir-report/ir-report-download.md`

## Global Constraints

- Color system: primary teal `#00566B`, text `#333`, secondary text `#666`, white. Neutral tints `#F5F7F9` (zebra) and `#DDD` (hairline rules) belong to the "neutral grays" bucket the spec's own table-standards section (5) prescribes verbatim — they are not counted as extra colors. The pre-rendered approval status-stamp images (green/amber/red raster assets, `StatusStampAssets`) are exempt from the max-4-colors rule — they are a status semantic, not document chrome, and the spec itself reserves red "exclusively for warnings/rejected statuses," which the rejected-status stamp already satisfies.
- Body 10.5pt / line-height 1.35. Section headings: 13pt bold, ALL CAPS, primary color, 18pt space above / 8pt below. No decorative borders on body pages (drop the current heading background fill + left border). Minimum font size 8pt anywhere.
- Never render `"Not Configured"`, `"undefined"`, `"null"`, `"test"`, or `"—"` as a value. Optional-and-missing → `"N/A"`. Required-and-missing (division head name, contact phone, letter ref, well ID) → **block generation entirely** (throw, no PDF produced).
- Table standards: solid primary-fill header (white bold 9pt caps), zebra `#F5F7F9`, hairline `0.5pt #DDD` rules, numbers right-aligned with consistent decimals, captions below the table at 8.5pt italic `#666`, numbered sequentially.
- Documented scope decisions (spec requirements this plan does **not** fully implement, and why):
  - **Lat/long coordinate labels** (spec example "N 25.4180, E 43.9002"): the data model only carries projected UTM easting/northing (meters), not geographic lat/long, and this codebase has no geodesy/reprojection capability. This plan applies the *spirit* of the rule (explicit unit labels, fixed decimal precision) to the existing UTM values rather than fabricating a reprojection.
  - **Contact phone**: no phone column is known to exist on the geologist-contact lookup (`GwdOpsMemberService` returns whatever an opaque Oracle proc's cursor contains, unverifiable from source). This plan sources the closing paragraph's phone number from a new **division-level** config property (defaulted to the Division's real published number, `872-8243`, already shown in the masthead), not a per-geologist number.
  - **Per-cell "N/A centered, gray" table styling**: achieving this exactly requires a Qute `{#if}` conditional on every one of the ~30 optional table cells across 4 tables. This plan guarantees the functional rule (never blank/dash, always literal `"N/A"`) but leaves cells left-aligned in the default text color — a minor visual polish item, not a defect, callable out as a fast follow if wanted.
  - **Multi-select bullet lists**: the fields named in spec section 1 (tests, sampling, development methods) are stored and returned as already-joined display strings (`stripped(header, "sampling")`, etc.) with no underlying array structure available in this assembler. No template change can turn a pre-joined string back into a bulleted list without a data-shape change upstream (out of scope here).
  - **CSS Paged-Media running header/footer** (`@top-center`/`@bottom-left`/`@bottom-right` margin boxes): iText's html2pdf module supports static-string margin-box `content` (already proven by the existing `@bottom-center` page-counter), so this plan implements it — but because the whole style block is wrapped in Qute's `{| ... |}` **raw** section (deliberately, so Qute's `{...}` parser doesn't choke on CSS braces), Qute variable interpolation cannot reach inside it directly. This plan works around that with literal placeholder tokens (`__RUNNING_HEADER__`, `__FOOTER_REF__`) substituted via plain `String.replace()` calls in `IrLetterService` after Qute renders and before the HTML is handed to the PDF renderer.
  - **Wellbore diagram SVG fidelity** (spec section 6: nested-casing cement hatch pattern, a labeled screen symbol, ≥9pt dark axis tick labels): per this plan's investigation, the client-rendered D3 diagram (Angular-Practice, `well-bore-view`/`wwell-ir-depth-scale` components) already draws nested concentric casings and a dashed/labeled static-water-level line, and its axis tick labels (20px/#000) already exceed the 9pt/#333 minimum — no change needed there. But it has **no cement hatch pattern** between casing strings (only a `gravelpattern` for Gravel Pack and a `gridPattern` of uncertain purpose) and no confirmed screen symbol. Task 8 adds a legend to the backend template that *labels* Cement/Screen swatches for a complete Figure 1 legend per spec, but the diagram image itself won't show a matching cement hatch until the Angular D3 casing renderer (`renderers/casing.renderer.ts`, `renderers/defs.renderer.ts`) is updated — that's frontend SVG work outside this plan's backend-only scope. Flagged here rather than silently claimed done; worth a short follow-up plan if the visual mismatch (labeled legend swatch with no matching pattern in the image) matters enough to fix now.

- [ ] **Step 3: Create the blocking exception**

`src/main/java/com/aramco/easd/gdsd/planning/exception/LetterGenerationBlockedException.java`:

```java
package com.aramco.easd.gdsd.planning.exception;

import jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response;

/** The IR letter is missing one or more fields the spec requires before a PDF may be produced at
 *  all (division head name, contact phone, letter ref, well ID) — maps to HTTP 422, distinct from
 *  a plain 400 InvalidRequestException since the request itself was valid; it's the underlying IR
 *  data that isn't ready for a letter yet. */
public class LetterGenerationBlockedException extends ApiException {

    public LetterGenerationBlockedException(String message) {
        super(Response.Status.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, message);
    }
}
```

Add the required-field constant and check method:

```java
    private static final String PLACEHOLDER_DIVISION_HEAD = "Division Head Name Not Configured";

    /** Package-private (not private) so the test above can call it directly without going through
     *  the full {@link #assemble} pipeline. Returns every missing field's human-readable name —
     *  the exception message lists all of them at once rather than failing one field at a time. */
    static List<String> missingRequiredFields(IrLetterData data) {
        List<String> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        if (isBlank(data.letterNumber())) {
            missing.add("Letter Reference");
        }
        if (isBlank(data.wellName())) {
            missing.add("Well ID");
        }
        if (isBlank(data.divisionHeadName()) || PLACEHOLDER_DIVISION_HEAD.equals(data.divisionHeadName())) {
            missing.add("Division Head Name");
        }
        if (isBlank(data.contactPhone())) {
            missing.add("Contact Phone");
        }
        return missing;
    }

    private static boolean isBlank(String value) {
        return value == null || value.isBlank();
    }
```

```java
        }
```


- [ ] **Step 4: Add `formatFixedDecimal` and apply it to the numeric well-location/hydrogeology fields**

Add the helper near `orNA`:

```java
    static String formatFixedDecimal(String raw, int decimals) {
        if (raw == null || raw.isBlank()) {
            return NOT_AVAILABLE;
        }
        try {
            return String.format("%." + decimals + "f", Double.parseDouble(raw.trim()));
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return NOT_AVAILABLE;
        }
    }
```

Apply it in `applyWellLocation(...)` (2 decimals — UTM survey precision) and `applyHydrogeology(...)` (water level/TDS keep 1 decimal, matching how they're already reported):

```java
    private static void applyWellLocation(IrLetterData.Builder b, Map<String, Object> well) {
        b.easting(formatFixedDecimal(str(well, "surfacee"), 2))
                .northing(formatFixedDecimal(str(well, "surfacen"), 2))
                .utmZone(orNA(str(well, "sv_utm_zn")))
                .elevationFt(formatFixedDecimal(str(well, "sv_surf_elevf"), 1));
    }

    private static void applyHydrogeology(IrLetterData.Builder b, Map<String, Object> hydrogeology) {
        b.aquifer(orNA(str(hydrogeology, "st_long_cd")))
                .waterLevelFt(formatFixedDecimal(str(hydrogeology, "est_sta_water_lvl"), 1))
                .tdsMgL(formatFixedDecimal(str(hydrogeology, "est_water_quality"), 1));
    }
```

Also apply 1-decimal formatting to `csg_depth`/`plan_tvd_dpth`/`plan_ss_dpth` in `toCasingRow`/`toTopsRow` — by this point Step 3's blanket rename has already turned these into `orNA(str(row, "..."))` calls; replace those specific three with `formatFixedDecimal(str(row, "..."), 1)`.

### Task 6: Letterhead reserved logo zone, bordered ref/date box, and the continuation-page running header

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/main/resources/templates/irLetter.html`
- Modify: `src/main/java/com/aramco/easd/gdsd/planning/service/IrLetterService.java`
- Test: `src/test/java/com/aramco/easd/gdsd/planning/service/IrLetterServiceTest.java` (new — the one piece of this task that's real logic: the placeholder-token substitution)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `IrLetterData.runningHeader()`, `.letterNumber()`, `.issueDate()` (Task 1).
- Produces: `IrLetterService.spliceCssContentToken(String xhtml, String token, String value)` (package-private static) — pure string function, unit-testable without touching CDI. Called twice: once for the top running header, once for the bottom-left footer ref/date (spec section 8's "every page" footer — the "Powered by AGWA" bottom-right mark needs no interpolation and is written as a plain literal in the CSS).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `src/test/java/com/aramco/easd/gdsd/planning/service/IrLetterServiceTest.java`:

```java
package com.aramco.easd.gdsd.planning.service;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class IrLetterServiceTest {

    @Test
    void replacesTheGivenTokenWithTheEscapedValue() {
        String xhtml = "content: \"__RUNNING_HEADER__\";";
        String result = IrLetterService.spliceCssContentToken(
                xhtml, "__RUNNING_HEADER__", "Groundwater Division · GWD: LTR1 · WELL_1");
        assertEquals("content: \"Groundwater Division · GWD: LTR1 · WELL_1\";", result);
    }

    @Test
    void escapesDoubleQuotesInTheValueSoTheCssStringStaysValid() {
        String xhtml = "content: \"__RUNNING_HEADER__\";";
        String result = IrLetterService.spliceCssContentToken(xhtml, "__RUNNING_HEADER__", "Well \"A\"");
        assertEquals("content: \"Well \\\"A\\\"\";", result);
    }

    @Test
    void replacesTwoDistinctTokensIndependently() {
        String xhtml = "content: \"__RUNNING_HEADER__\"; content: \"__FOOTER_REF__\";";
        String result = IrLetterService.spliceCssContentToken(xhtml, "__RUNNING_HEADER__", "Header");
        result = IrLetterService.spliceCssContentToken(result, "__FOOTER_REF__", "Ref: GWD-LTR1 · Issued Jan 1, 2026");
        assertEquals("content: \"Header\"; content: \"Ref: GWD-LTR1 · Issued Jan 1, 2026\";", result);
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run tests to verify they fail**

Run: `cd ~/Downloads/Misc/agwa-planning && ./mvnw -q -pl . test-compile -Dtest=IrLetterServiceTest`
Expected: FAIL — `spliceCssContentToken` does not exist yet.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `spliceCssContentToken` and call it from `renderLetterPdf`**

In `IrLetterService.java`, add:

```java
    /** The letter's `<style>` block is a Qute raw ({@code {| ... |}}) section so Qute's own
     *  {@code {...}} parser doesn't choke on CSS braces — which also means Qute can't interpolate
     *  {@code {letter.runningHeader}} inside it. Qute renders placeholder tokens below completely
     *  untouched (raw sections emit their text verbatim), so a plain post-render string
     *  substitution fills them in instead. Package-private + static so it's unit-testable without a
     *  CDI container. */
    static String spliceCssContentToken(String xhtml, String token, String value) {
        String escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"");
        return xhtml.replace(token, escaped);
    }
```

In `renderLetterPdf(...)`, splice both tokens before rendering to PDF:

```java
        String footerRef = "Ref: GWD-" + data.letterNumber() + " · Issued " + data.issueDate();
        String xhtml = letterTemplate.render(data).render();
        xhtml = spliceCssContentToken(xhtml, "__RUNNING_HEADER__", data.runningHeader());
        xhtml = spliceCssContentToken(xhtml, "__FOOTER_REF__", footerRef);
        byte[] pdf = HtmlToPdfRenderer.render(xhtml);
```
